newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Amsterdam bourse will survive EMU - chairman.
newsitem.headline: Amsterdam bourse will survive EMU - chairman.

text.p: The Amsterdam stock exchange will survive and even prosper as an independent bourse after the advent of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), chairman Boudewijn van Ittersum said on Thursday.
"I think all our endeavours are there to keep Amsterdam as an independent market after the introduction of the Euro," Van Ittersum said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
"We have finished a complete modernisation of trading and settlement systems and are now working on a merger with the options exchange in order to bring all our forces together."
"We are confident that when we have finished that programme, we will be strong enough to survive as an independent market."
Van Ittersum said the single currency could actually benefit the Dutch equity market.
"Presently, foreign investors are limited in investing in Dutch stocks because of the limited currency base of the guilder," he said.
"If we are part of a larger currency, that limitation will fall away and that means increased interest of foreign investors in the Dutch market."
Van Ittersum said that the exchange's recent recommendations for improving Dutch corporate governance would also, if implemented, make Dutch companies more attractive to foreign investors.
"I am confident that in the next two years, on the basis of these recommendations, there will be a significant improvement in shareholder relations in Holland," he said.
